oneOf.description: Replacement lobby has rendered its first usable frame.
Explicitly end the desktop party; a lobby disconnect is not a quit.
Retry the configured replacement lobby after a crash. Trusted local UI only.

Restart the host into the update named by `update_ready`, keeping the
party. Lobby only, and only between games.

Make `lobby` (one of the party's `lobbies`) the host's lobby and
restart into it, keeping the party. Local lobby UI only, between games.

The players whose phone is linked, replacing the previous list. Sent
by the host's web server, which pairs phones with players.
Only the authenticated lobby may publish physical input.
Opt into presence and live roster notifications for this prepared session.

Vibrate the controller on one of this session's seats. Games only, and
only while their session is running in front: a warm or paused game
is ignored. `weak` is the light high-frequency motor (surface, texture),
`strong` the heavy low one (impacts), each 0 to 65535 like XInput.
`ms` is how long it lasts (at most 5000); every message replaces the
previous one for that pad, so send short pulses repeatedly while the
effect should go on, and zero to stop at once.

Meaningful human input (deadzone filtered, at most once a second per device).
Games must supply their active session. Overlays omit it.
Must be the first message on every connection.

game.description: For `Role::Game`: which title this process runs.

token.description:
The launch token from `GAMENIGHT_TOKEN`. Required when the daemon
launched this process; omitted for manually started ones.

oneOf.description:
Walk in, grab a controller, press A. First free seat is yours — or ask
for a specific one with `seat` (falls back to the first free seat if
it's taken).

Add a player who plays on their phone and holds no controller. Takes
a free seat, or adds one past the controller seats (up to eight).

Change how a seated player's name reads everywhere (overlay, games
that show `players[].name`).
Change a player's accent-color hint (see [`Player::color`]).
Update a player's custom character pixel art avatar.

Tie a player to the profile behind them (`None` clears it), sent by
the host's web server when a profile is picked up. The value never
reaches games: they get a per-game [`Player::profile_key`] derived
from it.

Move a player to another place on the couch (see [`Player::couch`]),
shifting the people in between one place over. A position past the
end means the rightmost place.
Two people trade controllers: swap whoever sits in these two seats.
Physical gamepad's ordinal in the host's connected-controller list.
Move an existing entry without interrupting play. Reject stale snapshots.
Remove one occurrence only, guarded against concurrent playlist edits.
Skip to the warm session right now, no vote.

Make this game the next one up: it starts warming immediately
(inserted into the playlist after the current entry if needed).
Change the upcoming game without starting or resuming gameplay.
Add a new occurrence at the end, or first among upcoming games. Never starts play.
The party overlay came up: the active game pauses.
The overlay went away: resume, if it was the overlay that paused.
A player moves their avatar onto an option.

Pause, resume or skip the host's background music (see
[`NowPlaying`]). Ignored when nothing is playing — there is nothing
for the daemon to talk to.

Change a match setting. `game` defaults to the active game, so
"disable items" mid-match needs no lookup. The daemon validates the
value against the declared spec and pushes the change to the game.

Atomically validate a settings batch against a live session and revision.
Undo restores the last batch. Keep discards that undo snapshot.

Trusted local web server only: the complete current set of download
grants from the cloud, game id to token, for paid games someone
seated owns. Replaces the previous set; an empty map revokes all.
Tokens are secrets: never log or display them.

Trusted local web server only: preview builds the cloud lets this
table play, because someone seated owns or tests the game. The daemon
installs each one and puts it on the shelf as a playtest.
Assets loaded, controllers mapped — the session can start instantly.
A round ended. Informational: keep playing; no focus or playlist change.
Optional factual diagnostics, without accounts or recommendation data.

Optional: how far along warming is, so screens can show something
truthful while the party waits. Send as often as is useful; the
daemon keeps the latest. A game that loads instantly need never send
this — "loading" without a number is still a legitimate state.

percent.description: Whole percent, 0 to 100. Clamped by the daemon.

oneOf.description:
"Get me back to the party." Sent by a game when the player asks for
the lobby (a Back button, Backspace...). The daemon pauses this
session and gives the lobby the screen.

Games are not allowed to drive the party in general — this is the one
thing they may ask for, because a player stuck inside a game with no
way out is the one failure the party cannot recover from themselves.

"Somebody just asked for me." Sent by a game when a player reaches for
it directly rather than through the party — on the desktop that means
Cmd+Tab, a Dock click, a click on the window.

The pair to `request_overlay`, and the same bargain: the game reports
what the human did, the daemon decides what it means. Warm session ->
start it. Paused active session -> resume it. Anything else -> nothing
happens, and no harm done.

Focus is the one thing the party can always express and GameNight
cannot override — the window server has the final say. Taking it as a
statement of intent turns that from a fight into an instruction: the
game the party switched to is, by definition, the game they want.

Declare the match settings this game exposes. Send once after
`welcome` (and again after every reconnect). Replaces any previous
declaration; values the party already changed persist where they are
still valid under the new specs.

Offer a phone screen for this game (see [`CompanionScreen`]). Send
after `welcome`, and again after every reconnect. `root` must be an
absolute directory; `entry` is the page inside it. Declare a page,
an `app`, or both.

Opaque JSON between a game and phone screens. From a game, `player_id`
addresses one phone and its absence addresses every phone. From a
trusted overlay (the local web server), `game` names the recipient and
`player_id` the phone that sent it.

Game only: accept plain-text requests from players (see
[`GameCommands`]). Send after `welcome`, and again after reconnects.

Overlay only: `player_id` asks `game` for something in plain text, as
typed or spoken. The game answers with `command_result` and the same `id`.
Game only: the outcome of `game_command` `id`, in words for the player.
Overlay only: a player's phone screen for `game` connected or left.

download.description:
Where to get the app: an `https://` URL, or a file inside `root`
(such as `god.apk`), which the host then serves on the LAN.

name.description: Shown on the phone, e.g. "The Voice and the Will".

CompanionScreen.description:
A game's own phone screen: a small web page that GameNight serves to the
phones of seated players while that game is active, a native phone app,
or both. Games that support asymmetric play (a hidden hand of cards, a
god's-eye map) declare one with `declare_companion`; pages talk to the
game with `companion_message`, native apps use their own connection.

entry.description: Page to open, relative to `root`, e.g. `phone/index.html`.

root.description:
Absolute directory the local web server serves files from. Only
trusted local UIs see it; it is stripped from lobby snapshots.

ControllerState.description:
Physical input sampled by the lobby. Controller IDs are opaque host IDs,
never indexes into another process's device enumeration.

axes.description: left x/y, right x/y, left/right trigger; signed values / 32767.

buttons.description: A B X Y LB RB Back Start LS RS Up Down Left Right (bits 0..13).

GameCommands.description:
Plain-text requests a game accepts with `declare_commands`, such as
"geef me 10 End Crystal". Apps and the session assistant send them as
`game_command`; the game itself decides what they mean.

description.description:
What a player can ask for in plain words, for a person or an
assistant that turns speech into one of these requests.

examples.description: Requests the game understands as written, e.g. `geef me 10 End Crystal`.

GameId.description: Identifies a game *title* (e.g. `"towerfall"`), not a running instance.

GameIssueKind.description:
A stopped game process. Exit codes cannot reliably distinguish a forced
close from a crash; only label a known unsuccessful exit as unexpected.

GameMeta.description:
Presentation metadata for a title in the game library — everything an
overlay needs to sell the next game: cover art and all that.

best_players.description:
The count the game shines at, used to break ties between games that
all merely fit.

color.description: Accent color (`#rrggbb`) for generated covers and highlights.

cover.description:
Portrait cover: PNG data URI, or a shelf-relative PNG resolved by the
daemon. Web clients also support HTTPS artwork URLs.

icon.description: Square game icon (favicon), used on case spines.

launch.description:
How to start this game. Absent = the daemon waits for the process to
show up on its own (dev mode / externally managed).

min_phones.description:
Phones the game needs at the least among its players, for games where
only some play on a phone (one god on a phone, the rest on controllers).

min_players.description:
Human participants this game supports. Solo play with game-managed AI
is advertised with a minimum of one; a higher minimum does not imply
bot support. The daemon uses these bounds to warm
something that actually fits the party, so a shelf entry without them
is treated as "fits anything" rather than being skipped — an unknown
range should not make a game unplayable.

play_with.description:
What each player holds to play: a controller (the default), a phone,
both, or either. The player range above counts only the party members
who hold what this asks for.

players.description:
Human-readable player range, e.g. `"2–4"`. Display only — the daemon
picks games by `min_players`/`max_players`, never by parsing this.

screenshot.description: Gameplay screenshot, displayed on the lobby TV.

tagline.description: One-line pitch shown under the title.

GameSettings.description:
A game's declared settings plus their current values, as broadcast in
every [`PartySnapshot`]. Values are effective (defaults merged in) and
survive the game process reconnecting.

players.description: Each present player's effective values for the `player`-scoped specs.

InstallState.description:
Where a background install has got to. Distinct from `SessionPhase` on
purpose: a game being fetched has no process and no session, so none of
the session lifecycle applies to it — it isn't warming, it isn't loading,
it isn't on the shelf yet. It's arriving.

oneOf.description: In the queue, nothing happening yet.
Bytes are moving. This is the only state with a meaningful `percent`.
Downloaded; checking it against the catalogue's sha256.
Hash matched; unpacking it into place.
Playable. The shelf entry appears in the same snapshot.

Gave up. `label` carries why, because a party staring at a stalled
bar deserves to know whether to wait or pick something else.

InstallStatus.description:
One game arriving in the background, for any screen that wants to show
the party what's on its way.

Progress lives here rather than on `SessionInfo` because a download
happens *before* there is anything to have a session about — the process
doesn't exist, so it cannot report on itself the way a warming game does.

label.description: Human-readable detail — the failure reason, or a step's name.

percent.description:
Whole percent of the download, 0 to 100. Only `Downloading` sets it:
verifying and extracting are fast and their duration is unknowable,
so a bar for them would be a lie.

title.description:
The catalogue title, so a screen can name it without a shelf entry —
which by definition doesn't exist yet while this is downloading.

LaunchSpec.description:
How the daemon starts a game process. The handshake context (address,
game id, launch token) is passed via the `GAMENIGHT_*` environment
variables, not arguments, so unmodified binaries launch cleanly.

command.description: Executable path (absolute, or relative to the daemon's working dir).

env.description:
Extra environment for the process (the `GAMENIGHT_*` vars are added on
top and cannot be overridden here).

LobbyChoice.description: A lobby the host can run: bundled with the app or installed locally.

MediaAction.description:
What a player can ask of the host's music. Deliberately the three things
a room full of people actually shout about — no volume (that's the amp's
job and the host's call), no seeking, no library browsing.

oneOf.description:
Pause if playing, resume if paused — one pad, both jobs, because the
party can see which it is from the same card the pad sits under.

Start whatever the host played last, like the keyboard's Play key —
for the jukebox when nothing is on yet. Never pauses.

NowPlaying.description:
Music playing on the host machine, from whatever the person who's hosting
already had on — Spotify, Apple Music — read straight off the OS.

The party's music is part of the evening, not part of any game: somebody
puts a record on before the first match and it runs all night. Showing it
in the lobby (and letting anyone with a controller skip a track they hate)
means nobody has to walk to the host's laptop, which is the only reason
that laptop's owner ends up being the evening's DJ.

Absent from the snapshot entirely when nothing is on — see
`PartySnapshot::now_playing`.

artist.description:
Empty when the source doesn't know one (a podcast, a local file with
no tags) — screens should just show the title alone.

playing.description:
Whether it's actually making sound right now. A paused track still
appears, so the pad that paused it is also the pad that resumes it.

source.description:
Which app it's coming from ("Spotify"), so a screen can say where to
go when the party wants something this control surface can't do.

PartySnapshot.description: The one big object overlays render from. Sent whenever anything changes.

commands.description: Plain-text requests declared by connected games (see [`GameCommands`]).

companions.description: Phone screens declared by connected games (see [`CompanionScreen`]).

connected_games.description: Titles whose process is currently connected (playable right now).

game_issues.description:
Stopped processes awaiting an explicit retry. Takes precedence over
warming/loading hints. Runtime-owned, including failures before hello.

history.description: Games already played tonight, oldest first.

installs.description:
Games arriving in the background right now, most interesting first
(whatever is actually downloading leads). Empty once everything the
party might want is on disk.

Separate from `library`: these aren't playable yet, and showing them
as shelf entries would offer the party something it can't have.

library.description: The game shelf: every title the daemon knows, with cover art metadata.

lobbies.description:
Lobbies this host can switch to with `switch_lobby`, the running one
marked `current`. Empty when the host cannot switch (development runs).

next_game_index.description:
Exact upcoming playlist occurrence, including while its process launches.
Older hosts omit this; game IDs alone cannot distinguish duplicate entries.

now_playing.description:
What the host has on in the background, if anything.

`None` is the normal case — most nights nobody has music running, and
a lobby that shows an empty music card on those nights is worse than
one that shows none at all. Screens render this only when it's `Some`.

onboarding_error.description:
Host-owned failure of a requested first game. Cleared when resolved or
another game is chosen; never creates a synthetic library entry.

overlay_open.description:
Whether the party overlay is up. Opening it pauses the active game;
server-authoritative so every screen agrees.

phones.description:
Players with a phone linked to them, whichever way it joined. Games
that need phones count these (see [`PlayWith`]). A seat with a phone
and no controller is a phone-only player.

settings.description:
Match settings per game: what each title lets the party tweak, and
the current values. Only games that declared settings appear.

update_ready.description:
A newer version of the host app is downloaded and can be applied
with `apply_update` between games. The value is its version.

warming.description:
The game the daemon intends to have warm next, even before a session
for it exists — while its process is still launching, say.

Without this a screen can only see `warm_session`, so "still starting"
and "nothing to play" look identical, and guessing from the playlist
gets it wrong: the obvious guess is the first entry, which may be the
game that's already running.

PerformanceSample.description:
Optional cumulative application-frame diagnostics for this session.
Measure active frames only. Never send serial numbers, paths or machine names.

PlayWith.description:
What a player needs in hand to play a game. A phone counts once its owner
has linked it to their player (`PartySnapshot::phones`).

oneOf.description: A controller. Phones may still open the game's phone screen.
A phone; controllers are not needed (cards, trading, private choices).
A controller and a phone each.

Either: asymmetric games where some play on a phone, the rest on a
controller. Pair with `min_phones`.

avatar.description:
Pixel art the player drew for themselves in the studio.

Opaque on the wire so the encoding can evolve without a protocol
bump — decode it with [`Avatar::parse`] rather than reading the
string directly, and games get RGBA they can upload as a texture.
See the [`avatar`] module for the format.

color.description:
Game-controlled clothing/team colour (`#rrggbb`). Games may override
it without changing the personal `skin_color` preference.

couch.description:
Where this player sits on the couch, counted from the left (0 is the
leftmost). Every player in the party has a distinct position; players
change it from their Start menu in the lobby, also during a match
(`players_updated`). Order split-screen views and anything else laid
out left to right by it, not by seat: a seat is a controller slot.
Sort by it rather than indexing with it, since a session's players
may be a part of the party. Older hosts leave it out.

library.description: Games owned in this player's profile library, shared with the party.

profile_key.description:
Stable key for the person behind this player, for saving their own
settings, progress and world data between nights. Different for every
game, so two games cannot match up their players; never an account id.
Only sent to games, and only for players with a profile (a signed-in
account or a remembered local profile). Guests have none: keep their
data for the night only.

skin_color.description: Personal skin colour (#rrggbb), independent of game/team clothing colours.

PlayerId.description: A player in the party. Stable for the lifetime of the party, across games.

current.description: Index of the entry the *active* session is playing, if any.

queued.description:
How many entries right after `current` players queued themselves, in
the order they asked. Everything after those is autoplay: games the
host recommends so the queue never runs dry.

Playtest.description: One game's playtest, as the cloud's room poll hands it to a host.

entry.description: The catalogue entry for the preview build, downloads included.

grant.description: Unlocks this game's preview downloads. A secret: never log it.

versions.description: The preview's version on each platform, for the shelf.

PresenceState.description: Presence is separate from identity: sleeping never releases a seat.

Role.description: The role a connection announces in its `hello`.

oneOf.description: A game process (via an SDK). Receives session lifecycle commands.

The configured replacement lobby. Uses one authenticated connection
for party commands, snapshots, focus and runtime-owned input.
An overlay / controller UI. Receives party snapshots, sends commands.

Seat.description:
A playable position. Seat indices are stable across games so player 2 stays
player 2 all night.

controller.description:
Opaque platform hint (e.g. `"xinput:0"`). Games should not need it; the
daemon owns input routing.

SeatOccupant.description: Who (or what) fills a seat. Games receive seats, never raw controller ids.

oneOf.description: A player on this machine.
A player connected over the network (future phase, already on the wire).
A bot fills the seat.
Nobody. Games may hide or skip empty seats.
Full controller snapshot, including neutral/released state.

Full authoritative roster/presence for an opted-in session. Apply without
resetting the match. Unknown fields/messages remain optional for old games.

Players of this session changed their details: name, colour, skin,
face or `profile_key` (someone picked up a profile in the lobby). The
same people in the same seats, so apply it to the running match: never
restart or reset over it. Sent to every active session, opted in or
not, with the players it was prepared with.
Reply to `hello`.

godot_sdk.description: The Godot addon version this host ships; older copies warn.

oneOf.description: Broadcast to overlays whenever party state changes.
Warm up: load assets, map the given seats, then reply `ready`.
Become the active game *now*. Sent only after `ready`.
Tear everything down; the session id will never be used again.

Sent only to the requesting overlay after an accepted settings batch.
A host acknowledgement, not proof that a next-round change is in play.

A match setting changed; sent to the game that declared it. Apply it
live if a match is running, otherwise from the next match. Also sent
after `declare_settings` for every value the party had already
changed from its default (reconnect re-hydration).

One player's effective values for every `player`-scoped setting the
game declared (defaults merged in). Sent after `declare_settings`,
with every `prepare` and `party_updated`, and whenever the player or
their profile changes one.

Sent to the persistent lobby game specifically (see
`GameNight::set_lobby_game`) — `active: false` the moment some other
game actually starts, so the lobby can mute itself and step out of
the way; `true` once the party's back with nothing else running. Not
session-scoped: the lobby never has a tracked session of its own to
hang this off of.

Phone screen traffic. To a game: `player_id` is the phone that sent
`data`. To overlays: `game` sent it, and `player_id` is the phone it is
for (absent means every phone showing that game).

To a game: a plain-text request from `player_id` (see
`declare_commands`). Answer with `command_result` and the same `id`.
To overlays: what a game answered to `game_command` `id`.

To a game: a player's phone screen connected or went away. A game
sends that player its current view when `connected` is true.
Something was rejected. Informational; connections stay open.

rounds_reported.description: Number of `finished` reports received, not proof every round was reported.

SessionId.description: A single playable game instance. Sessions are disposable; ids are not reused.

diagnostics.description: Host lifecycle counters for status displays and diagnostics. Not a rating.

progress.description:
How far along loading is, 0 to 100, if the game bothers to say.
Optional on purpose: a game that loads instantly has nothing to
report, and screens must stay honest without it (see `Progress`).

Whole percent rather than a fraction — it's what screens display, and
it keeps every type on the wire comparable.

progress_label.description: What it's doing right now ("generating arena"), if the game says.

SessionPhase.description: Session lifecycle. Legal transitions are enforced by `gamenight-core`.

SettingKind.description:
What kind of knob a setting is, its default, and what values it accepts.
Flattened into [`SettingSpec`] on the wire (`"kind": "toggle"`, …).

oneOf.description: On/off.
An integer in `min..=max` (stock count, time limit, score cap).
One of a fixed set of options (arena, game mode).
One value for the whole party.
Each player their own value.

SettingSpec.description: One knob a game exposes to the party.

oneOf.description: On/off.
An integer in `min..=max` (stock count, time limit, score cap).
One of a fixed set of options (arena, game mode).

description.description:
What the knob does — worth writing well: this is what overlays show
and what an LLM reads to map "disable items" onto a key.

key.description: Stable identifier (`"items"`, `"stock"`). Unique within the game.

scope.description:
`player`: every player has their own value (their character, their
stick sensitivity), saved with their profile between nights. Sent with
`player_settings`, changed with `set_player_setting`. Default `party`:
one value for everyone.

SettingValue.description: A match-setting value on the wire: plain JSON scalars, no tagging.

VoteOption.description: End-of-game options players stand on with their avatars.

decided.description: Set once consensus is reached; cleared when the next vote opens.

open.description:
Whether the party is currently being asked to choose.

Without this, a screen cannot tell "waiting for you to vote" from
"nothing happening": after a game finishes the night stops until the
seated players pick, and a lobby with no way to say so just looks
stuck.

positions.description: Which option each player currently stands on.

description: One JSON object per WebSocket text frame, tagged by "type". Generated from crates/gamenight-protocol; do not edit.
title: GameNight wire protocol
